sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by anti-myc immunofluorescence (L5) and cell-surface fraction Western blot (L7) in HEK293T cells. Transfection efficiency (% myc-positive cells) measured for WT and histidine-mutant constructs (L6). pH-dependent function of the WT-myc construct itself is NOT MEASURED in the cited clips; functional assays in L6 concern histidine mutants, not the tag per se.
sites.rationale: GPR4 has a single extracellular terminus: the N-terminal span (residues 1–17, extracellular per topology landmarks), which is 17 residues from TM1 (beginning at residue 18), well beyond the 3-residue minimum. The C-terminus (residues 290–362) is intracellular, so surface detection of myc by non-permeabilized immunofluorescence and cell-surface biotinylation/WB (L5–L7) uniquely localises the tag to the N-terminal prepend position (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M). This is topology_derived because no residue number is stated in the clips. L8 provides corroborating indirect precedent: the closest paralog OGR1/GPR68 tolerates a 3×FLAG tag inserted 'in front of' its coding sequence (i.e., N-terminal prepend) in a functional knock-in. L5/L6/L7 (PMC11376338): Full-length mGPR4-myc constructs expressed in HEK293T cells; anti-myc immunofluorescence detects surface-positive cells (L5, L6), and a biotinylation-based cell-surface Western blot probed with anti-myc confirms myc accessibility on the extracellular face (L7). No residue number is stated. GPR4's C-terminus is intracellular (residues 290–362 per topology landmarks), leaving the N-terminal extracellular span (residues 1–17) as the only extracellular terminus; the tag must therefore be prepended before residue 1. Additional indirect support from L8 (PMC2684630): a 3×FLAG tag inserted 'in front of' OGR1 (GPR68), the closest proton-sensing paralog of GPR4, at its N-terminus in a knock-in construct.

sources.claim: A , Representative images of WT and histidine mutant GPR4-myc constructs expressed in HEK293T cells; scale bar, 30 µm.

literature_notes: L1–L4 (PMC10928412) all describe a C-terminal HA tag (GSSG-YPYDVPDYA) on GPR4, validated by cAMP assay (L2) and in vivo hypercapnic ventilatory response (L3). This tag is functionally silent and robustly validated, but the C-terminus of GPR4 is intracellular (residues 290–362 per topology landmarks); it therefore cannot serve as an extracellular surface tag site and is recorded in other_positions. L8 (PMC2684630) describes an N-terminal 3×FLAG on OGR1/GPR68 (close paralog); this is indirect evidence for GPR4 and points to the same N-terminal prepend position already grounded in L5–L7, so no additional site is added. No ledger line pins a tag to any of the three extracellular loops (ECL1 75–87, ECL2 155–177, ECL3 247–266) of GPR4.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag (GSSG-YPYDVPDYA) appended after the last residue Q362; functionally silent in pH-dependent cAMP assay (HEK293T) and in vivo HCVR (knock-in mice), but the C-terminus lies in the intracellular domain (residues 290–362) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
